summary:
Dancing with the SARs – Explore Earth. Understand Change.

Dancing with the SARs is an interactive web application developed by our mother-son team, Satellite Finders, to make NISAR satellite radar observations easier to explore and understand. The application connects to NASA's Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) data service, allowing users to select a date, location, and data product (GUNW or GCOV) to search for available NISAR observations. It displays available satellite browse images along with important observation details. The website also includes a Learning Centre that explains NISAR's mission, radar technology, L-band and S-band, and how radar images help us study Earth's surface.

Our project addresses the challenge by making real satellite data more accessible and understandable, especially for students and beginners. It is important because understanding changes on Earth through satellite observations can support learning, research, and awareness of our dynamic planet.
details:
Project Details – Dancing with the SARs

Team: Satellite Finders

Dancing with the SARs is an interactive web application developed by our mother-son team to make real NISAR satellite radar observations easier to access, explore, and understand. Our project focuses on helping students, beginners, and anyone interested in Earth science discover how radar satellites observe our changing planet.

How does it work?

Users can select a date, choose a location on an interactive map, and select a NISAR data product: GUNW or GCOV. The application connects to NASA's Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) data service and searches for available NISAR observations matching the selection. It displays the available browse images and observation details. The website also includes a Learning Centre with explanations of the NISAR mission, radar technology, L-band and S-band, radar image interpretation, and the differences between GUNW and GCOV products.

Benefits and intended impact

NISAR data can be complex for beginners to understand. Our project provides a simple, educational interface that helps users explore actual satellite observations. It encourages interest in space science, remote sensing, Earth monitoring, and scientific data exploration. Our long-term vision is to help people understand how satellite observations can contribute to studying floods, earthquakes, agriculture, glaciers, and other changes on Earth.

Tools and technologies used

  • Python – application logic and data processing
  • Flask – web application framework
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript – website structure, design, and interactivity
  • Leaflet.js – interactive location selection map
  • NASA Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) API – searching real NISAR observations
  • Git and GitHub – source-code management
  • Render – web hosting and deployment
  • Custom domain – sajanverse.earth

Creativity and innovation

Our creative approach is to combine a satellite data explorer with a student-friendly Learning Centre in one website. Instead of simply presenting satellite images, we allow users to choose locations, dates, and radar data products and learn what those products represent. We named our project Dancing with the SARs to represent the continuous changes and movements happening across Earth's surface.

Factors considered

We considered ease of use, scientific accuracy, accessibility of open satellite data, internet connectivity, availability of browse images, and the learning needs of beginners. We also designed the application using free and accessible development tools so that it can be explored without expensive equipment.

Through this project, we hope to make satellite science more approachable and inspire more students to explore space technology and understand our changing planet.
